answers.gloss: A traffic-engineering node in a per-layer network; it is the topological/forwarding node abstraction used by the TE topology.
answers.example: ROADM R1 represented as a node in the OTN-layer TE topology.
answers.relations: It is part of i.tetopo. Its i.tp termination points and i.cmatrix switching constraints are on the node; i.telink objects run between such nodes.

answers.gloss: A node-owned termination point at which a TE link terminates.
answers.example: tp-R1-R2 on R1, terminating the R1–R2 TE link.
answers.relations: It is on i.tenode and terminates i.telink. A TP can participate in a server/client supporting relationship represented by i.stp.

answers.gloss: The supporting relationship by which a client-layer TP is supported by a server-layer TP; it represents inter-layer adaptation/support rather than an ordinary same-layer link.
answers.example: An OTN TP at R1 supported by an optical-layer TP at R1.
answers.relations: It relates supporting and supported i.tp objects across layers. It preserves node-local layer adaptation and is not itself a TE link between distinct nodes.

answers.gloss: The point at which a TE tunnel originates or terminates—a tunnel trail head.
answers.example: The A1 tunnel termination point at the head of the A1–A3 ODU2 tunnel.
answers.relations: It is on i.tenode and originates or terminates i.tunnel. It is a tunnel endpoint, not inherently an externally exposed service-access point; external exposure would require additional semantics absent from this concept.

answers.gloss: An end-to-end traffic-engineered tunnel that realizes connectivity for a service.
answers.example: The A1–A3 ODU2 tunnel engineered across the OTN network.
answers.relations: It runs between i.ttp tunnel termination points, is engineered over i.tetopo, can have node-local i.tcep endpoints, and may be labelled by i.otnlabel. It is an internal TE construct that realizes service connectivity, not necessarily the offered service contract itself.

answers.gloss: An OTN label that expresses the tributary-slot multiplexing structure used to carry a client ODU in a server signal.
answers.example: The TS/TPN selection for carrying an ODU2 within an OTU4.
answers.relations: It labels i.tunnel and identifies its OTN tributary-slot allocation/multiplex structure. It is technology-specific switching-resource information, not merely a generic statement that one layer protocol is supported by another.

answers.gloss: The matrix of permitted internal connectivity within a TE node.
answers.example: R2's connectivity matrix specifying which ingress and egress termination points may be cross-connected.
answers.relations: It is on i.tenode and constrains permitted internal cross-connectivity among that node's termination points.

answers.gloss: A traffic-engineering link between TE nodes in one layer network.
answers.example: The R1–R2 TE link in the OTN-layer topology.
answers.relations: It runs between i.tenode objects, is terminated by node-owned i.tp objects, and is contained in i.tetopo.

answers.gloss: A per-layer traffic-engineering network/topology.
answers.example: The OTN-layer TE network containing R1, R2, R3 and their OTN TE links.
answers.relations: It contains i.tenode and i.telink objects and provides the topology over which i.tunnel is engineered. This concept is layer-specific rather than a single intrinsically multi-layer topology, although relationships between layers can be represented through support/adaptation.

answers.gloss: An endpoint of a tunnel connection within a node.
answers.example: The connection endpoint for the A1–A3 tunnel on R1.
answers.relations: It is on i.tenode and is part of i.tunnel. It denotes a connection/tunnel endpoint internal to the network model, not an ordinary TE-link termination point or an external service interface.

answers.gloss: A forwarding/topological node in the domain's single multi-layer TAPI topology.
answers.example: ROADM R1.
answers.relations: It is part of t.topo. Node-owned t.ltp, t.sip, and t.cep points, node-local t.translink adaptations, and t.nrg switching constraints are associated with it; t.link objects connect nodes.

answers.gloss: A node-owned edge point at which a topological link terminates.
answers.example: The R1 edge point facing R2, nep-R1-R2.
answers.relations: It is on t.node and terminates t.link. It represents a link-facing node edge, unlike the service-facing t.sip and connection-specific t.cep.

answers.gloss: A node-local construct expressing adaptation between signal layers, rather than an ordinary link between distinct nodes.
answers.example: The OTU4-to-ODU2 adaptation at R1.
answers.relations: It is at t.node and expresses adaptation involving the multiplex/layer structure described by t.lpq. Its intended role is inter-layer transition, while t.link provides inter-node topology connectivity.

answers.gloss: A point where an external client service accesses the network.
answers.example: The externally exposed ODU2 client hand-off at A1, sip-A1-odu.
answers.relations: It is on t.node and is used by t.cs. It is specifically service-facing: unlike t.ltp it does not merely terminate a topology link, and unlike t.cep it is not merely an internal endpoint of a realized connection.

answers.gloss: An offered end-to-end connectivity service across the network.
answers.example: The A1-to-A3 ODU2 connectivity service, cs-a1a3-odu2.
answers.relations: It uses t.sip access points, is realized by connection endpoints t.cep, is qualified by t.lpq, and runs over t.topo. It denotes the service abstraction rather than merely an internal engineered tunnel.

answers.gloss: A qualifier describing the layer protocol and multiplexing/mapping structure of a signal.
answers.example: ODU2 mapped into an OTU4 server signal.
answers.relations: It qualifies t.cs and is referenced by the adaptation semantics of t.translink. It states layer and multiplex structure; it does not specifically identify an allocated tributary-slot/TPN switching resource.

answers.gloss: A node rule group constraining which ports or edge points may be internally cross-connected.
answers.example: The permitted ingress-to-egress cross-connect combinations on R2.
answers.relations: It is on t.node and governs node-internal switching connectivity. Its granularity is a group of cross-connect rules among the relevant node ports/edge points.

answers.gloss: A topological link between two forwarding nodes in the domain topology.
answers.example: link-R1-R2 between R1 and R2.
answers.relations: It runs between t.node objects, is terminated by node-owned t.ltp objects, and is contained in the multi-layer t.topo.

answers.gloss: The single multi-layer topology describing the whole domain.
answers.example: The OTN-over-optical domain containing its packet/OTN/optical forwarding abstractions as applicable.
answers.relations: It contains t.node and t.link objects and is the topology over which t.cs is provided. Unlike a per-layer topology object, this concept intrinsically represents the domain in one multi-layer topology.

answers.gloss: An endpoint of a realized connection within a node.
answers.example: The endpoint for the A1-A3 connection on R1, cep-a1a3-R1.
answers.relations: It is on t.node and participates in realizing t.cs. It is connection-specific, unlike the link-facing t.ltp, and it is not the externally exposed service access represented by t.sip.

proposals.rationale: Both denote a forwarding/topological node abstraction containing termination points and switching constraints and participating in topological links. The topology containers differ in layering organization, but the node meanings coincide.
Both are node-owned edge/termination points at which topological or TE links terminate.
Both encode node-local constraints on which ingress and egress ports or termination points may be internally cross-connected.

Both are inter-node topological traffic-engineering links terminated by node-owned link termination points. B organizes them in per-layer topologies whereas A places them in one multi-layer topology, but the link abstraction is the same.

Both denote a connection-specific endpoint within a node, illustrated by the endpoint of the same A1-A3 engineered connectivity. Their parent constructs are described at different abstraction levels, but neither is a link TP or external service interface.
